In each round a linear scorer gives every token a score, a masked softmax turns the scores into weights, and those weights pool the current residual token states into an "atom". The same weights also pool the original states, and these pooled originals are mixed with learned weights to form the value. Each round then deflates the line: it takes the unit direction of the atom and removes that direction from every token state by orthogonal projection, which is one step of Gram–Schmidt (a matching-pursuit-style step). After the rounds, a learned r=12 basis is orthonormalised with QR, and its subspace is projected out of the remaining residual states. Each token gets a score equal to α·log of its remaining energy, plus a learned cue from its original state. A softmax over these scores pools the off-subspace residuals into a final "novelty" atom. The key is a linear map of all the gain-scaled atoms joined together. The value is a linear map of the mixed pools of original states.

DESCRIPTION: The module takes the masked token states of one line and builds a retrieval key from several pooled summaries, then adds fixed projections on top. (1) **Deflation pursuit:** K softmax attention pools run one after another. After each pool, the module removes that pooled direction from every token, so the next pool only sees what is left (a Gram-Schmidt / matching-pursuit step). (2) **Novelty pool:** a learned rank-r subspace is orthonormalised with QR. Each token gets a score equal to the fraction of its energy that lies outside that subspace, and an attention pool runs over these out-of-subspace parts. (3) **Distinctiveness pool:** tokens are pooled with scores that rise when a token is unlike the rest of the line (low mean cosine and low soft-max cosine to other tokens). The input to this pool is the line's centred token states. A second "conjunction" pool uses the product of the novelty and distinctiveness weights. (4) **Sinkhorn slots:** 6 log-domain Sinkhorn iterations compute an entropic optimal-transport plan. It moves token mass (from learned "mass" scores) onto S learned prototype slots of equal mass, with cost set by cosine similarity, and each slot is the transport-weighted sum of tokens. (5) **Key:** all the pooled vectors are concatenated and passed through one linear layer. Then an "echo" is added, scaled by the key's norm: the unit-normalised distinctiveness, conjunction and slot vectors, each projected through a fixed, non-trainable random isometry. (6) **Value:** a linear map of the sum of the pursuit atoms, plus an optional second linear map of the first atom.
